analysis: The supplied change is to docs/architecture/inference.md only. It bumps the 'Last updated' date, and adds text saying a serial-prefill Gemma 4 pipeline (coordinator-installed or local) starts at its installed default lane width instead of one. The patch excerpt shows only part of the change (it is truncated, and further hunks near lines 4483-4538 and 4901-4927 are not in the supplied patch text), so I could not review those. I examined the base excerpt at lines 5337-5436 and the head excerpt at lines 1-420, covering the automatic batching, cluster setup, Nemotron Super and video-ingest sections. These are documentation only, with no executable code, key handling, authorization, attestation or encryption changes. The only security-adjacent prose is the Gemma 4 pipeline width change. It describes a lane default (a throughput and memory setting) and does not touch the TB-002 coordinator-provider trust boundary, the TB-011 authorization, A-016 serving authorization, or the T-041 prefix cache. It states that explicit diagnostic and lane settings keep their choice and that existing per-request admission and LOAD memory safeguards remain authoritative. One open question: the docs now say the Gemma 4 pipeline default lane count exceeds one. Whether the code enforces per-request isolation and memory bounds at that width (and cross-request prefix-cache or KV isolation, T-028/T-041) cannot be checked from these docs-only units. The corresponding code changes, if any, are in other batches and need review there. No finding is raised because no unsafe behavior is shown in the supplied text.
